questions.situation: You hear two friends discussing a weekend walking trip.
questions.prompt: What has caused a difficulty for the women's plans?
options: A) Unexpectedly bad weather in the forecast
B) A problem with transport to the starting point
C) The person who was going to provide equipment can no longer do so
questions.script:
A: I'm absolutely gasping for a weekend away — work's been piling up all month and I simply can't switch off once I'm home.
B: Same here, though if the mist rolls in on Sunday morning, we may have to call the ridge walk off altogether.
A: The forecast looks settled enough for now, touch wood. What really bothers me is we still haven't sorted out who's bringing the camping stove.
B: Liam was going to look into hiring one from the outdoor shop on Mill Lane — he'd even gone as far as getting a quote.
A: Well, he's had to pull out at short notice because his dad's been taken into hospital, so unless one of us steps in and gets hold of something, we'll be stuck with cold food on the summit.

questions.situation: You hear an announcement at a ferry terminal.
questions.prompt: What are passengers told to do?
options: A) Stay in the terminal until check-in opens
B) Join the queue at lane four as quickly as possible
C) Collect their vehicles from the car park before midday
questions.script: Attention passengers travelling on the midday Dover crossing. Please note that check-in will not open until twelve o'clock sharp due to temporary staffing shortages on the ground floor. Remain inside the terminal building at all times and do not proceed to vehicle lane four, where queuing is not permitted at this time. Updated departure information will be announced through the loudspeakers once boarding procedures begin. Vehicle passengers must ensure passports and booking references are ready for inspection at the desk. We apologise sincerely for the inconvenience caused and thank you for your patience while we get things back to normal.

questions.situation: You hear a woman telephoning a dental surgery.
options: A) To arrange to be seen about a dental problem she has been ignoring
B) To cancel an appointment she can no longer attend
C) To complain about a temporary repair that has come loose
questions.script:
A: Good morning, Riverside Dental Surgery — how can I help you today?
B: Hi, it's Rachel Masters. I need an appointment — I've been putting off a proper check-up for ages, and now I've got sharp pain whenever I bite down on anything firm.
A: The earliest routine slot is three weeks away, I'm afraid. I can put you down for emergency triage tomorrow at half past four — just bring your NHS number.
B: Tomorrow works — I'd rather get it sorted properly once and for all than have something temporary done that might come loose again.
A: Could you arrive ten minutes early to fill in the medical history form?

questions.situation: You hear two flatmates talking about their washing machine.
questions.prompt: What do the men decide to do about the washing machine?
options: A) Report the fault and wait for the agency to send someone official
B) Look online for a replacement appliance they can install themselves
C) Try getting it repaired locally rather than buying a new one
questions.script:
A: Have you seen the washing machine? It cut out mid-cycle again last night without warning.
B: I noticed — it left my gym kit sitting in soapy water for hours, and the whole flat smelled damp.
A: I had a look at the filter, but I can't get the back panel off without the right tool. I rang the letting agency, and they said minor breakdowns are down to us to sort out ourselves.
B: We could try that repair shop on Garston Road — they fixed my mate's dryer last year, and he said they didn't rip him off.
A: Worth a shot before we shell out on a new one. Just don't go ahead and order anything online — we can't afford that right now.

questions.situation: You hear a recorded message from a gym.
questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the message?
options: A) To confirm that the woman's membership has already been cancelled
B) To find out whether the woman still intends to remain a member
C) To tell her about a lower-cost membership she may want to consider
questions.script: Hi, it's Grace calling from FitWorks on behalf of the membership team. Your annual membership comes up for renewal next Friday, and I wanted to touch base before anything goes through automatically. We've brought in a new off-peak tariff that works out considerably cheaper if you mainly train before six in the evening. I know you mentioned you'd let your contract run out because you were relocating down south, but your file still shows your old address on Church Street. If you're staying in the area, pop in and we can talk you through the options — otherwise, give us a ring back so we don't keep charging you by mistake. Could you get back to us before the end of the week?

questions.situation: You hear a conversation in a bookshop.
questions.prompt: What does the man offer to do?
options: A) Order a book that is not currently available in the shop
B) Check whether another branch has the book in stock today
C) Recommend a similar novel from the display by the window
questions.script:
A: Can I help at all?
B: I'm trying to track down a novel for my mum — she read a review in the paper, but I've drawn a blank online.
A: Was it historical fiction? We've got new releases by the window if that rings any bells.
B: It's set in Belfast in the seventies — the title had "bridge" in it, but I might be mixing it up.
A: That rings a bell — we sold out last week, but I could order a copy in. It takes four or five days to come through.
B: Perfect — she'll be chuffed if it arrives before her birthday.

questions.situation: You hear two colleagues talking about a charity run.
questions.prompt: What do the women agree to do?
options: A) Train together every weekend until the day of the event
B) Share one online page to collect donations from supporters
C) Ask their employer to match whatever they manage to raise
questions.script:
A: You're still up for the charity run at the end of the month, aren't you? I only signed up because you talked me into it.
B: Definitely — I'm gradually building up my distance on the routes round the park. The really tricky bit is hitting the fundraising target the organisers set.
A: I put off setting up my sponsorship page for weeks. People kept asking for the link on social media and I had nothing worthwhile to share.
B: If we put together a joint page, we can get the message out in one go — that way nobody ends up pestering the same friends twice.
A: Good shout. I'll get on to that tonight before I talk myself out of it altogether.

questions.situation: You hear a tenant speaking to a letting agent on the phone.
questions.prompt: What does the agent advise the tenant to do?
options: A) Withhold part of the rent until the neighbour removes the equipment
B) Keep a written record of when the disturbance happens
C) Arrange a meeting with the neighbour without involving the agency
questions.script:
A: Hi, it's Priya from the agency — following up on your email about next door.
B: Thanks for ringing back. Bass comes through the wall at night — hard to switch off and sleep.
A: I've spoken to your neighbour. He'll turn the volume down after eleven, but won't rip the speakers out.
B: That's a start, but it doesn't get to the bottom of it.
A: We can't take formal steps unless it's been properly logged over several weeks. Keep a written record — we'll review at month-end.
B: OK — I'll note the dates and times from tonight.
